top_stories.title: Kaynes shares plunge 43% from October peak. Is a tactical rebound on the cards or more pain ahead? - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Anand James**, Chief Market Strategist at **Geojit Investments Limited**, suggests a potential short-term downward trend in the Nifty, with support levels around 26,085–26,065.  The IT sector is expected to continue its upward momentum, potentially reaching 39,500, while PSU banks may experience a pullback early next week. **COFORGE** and **ABCAPITAL** are recommended as potential buy opportunities with targets of 2,080-2180 and 368-377 respectively.

top_stories.title: FPIs pull out Rs 27,000 cr in May; 2026 outflows hit Rs 2.2 lakh cr-mark - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)** have withdrawn a record **Rs 2.2 lakh crore** from the Indian equity market in 2026, exceeding the total outflows of **Rs 1.66 lakh crore** in 2025.  **Himanshu Srivastava**, Principal - Manager Research at Morningstar Investment Research India, attributed this trend to global growth uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and volatility in crude oil prices, which have dampened risk appetite towards emerging markets. **V K Vijayakumar**, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, highlighted the impact of sustained FPI selling on the rupee's depreciation, potentially reaching 96 to the US dollar.  He also noted that capital flows into AI-focused companies are diverting funds away from India.

top_stories.title: There is a leadership vacuum in Infosys, time to get Nandan Nilekani back: Mohandas Pai - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Mohandas Pai**, former Infosys Board Member, believes the recent high-profile exits are a result of leadership vacuum and poor chemistry within the company. He suggests that the board needs to address this issue by appointing a new CEO with experience in enterprise management and fostering a strong connection between Nandan Nilekani, the executive chairman, and the next generation of leaders.  Pai also believes that some bloodletting is necessary for the company's future success and that external expertise may be needed.

top_stories.title: Our commitment for press freedom, and autonomy of public broadcast is absolute: Prakash Javadekar - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The Minister of state (independent charge) for information and broadcasting, environment and climate change, **Prakash Javadekar**, has outlined the government's approach to communication and media. The new **I&B** ministry will establish a social media hub to manage all ministers' social media outreach, including Facebook, Twitter, and other platforms.  The ministry aims to enhance transparency, effectiveness, and accessibility within the government's communications strategy.  **Javadekar** also emphasized the importance of public broadcaster autonomy while addressing concerns about potential media control. He highlighted the need for synergy between ministries and a focus on learning from the new government's approach to communication.

top_stories.title: Raamdeo Agarwal: We may see rapid growth over the next few years: Raamdeo Agrawal - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Raamdeo Agrawal**, Joint Managing Director of **Motilal Oswal Financial Services**, believes the Indian economy is poised for a multi-year bull run due to a new government with clear mandates and potential for strong economic growth. He acknowledges that while there are challenges, such as inflation and supply chain issues, the market has yet to fully price in the positive changes brought about by the new government.  **Agrawal** suggests investors should focus on companies with solid fundamentals and avoid low-quality stocks, emphasizing patience and long-term investment strategies for potential gains.

top_stories.title: Confidence level of industry improving: KV Kamath, ICICI Bank - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **KV Kamath**, Chairman of ICICI Bank, believes the Indian economy will see growth in the first term of the current government. He anticipates a fiscal discipline approach in the upcoming budget and sees corporate investment picking up within three to six months. **Kamath** also expects a positive impact from reforms addressing stalled projects and monetary policy adjustments driven by fiscal discipline.  He predicts that interest rates could begin to decline within the next 12 months, potentially starting with a quarter percentage point reduction in the first half of the year.

top_stories.title: Narendra Modi has his eyes set on boosting business: Joao Cravinho, EU Ambassador - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ambassador Joao Cravinho**, head of the **European Union** delegation in India, met with **Narendra Modi** during his time as Gujarat Chief Minister.  He believes that the new Prime Minister has a clear vision for India and governance, and that EU member states have the potential to drive economic growth in India. The EU is already the largest trading partner and source of foreign direct investment for India. Cravinho expressed confidence that the FTA negotiations will benefit India and hopes for progress before the next India-EU Summit at Brussels.

top_stories.title: Every decision of government needn’t be a big reform: Anand Mahindra - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Anand Mahindra**, chairman and MD of **Mahindra & Mahindra**, expressed optimism about the new Indian government's 10-point agenda, particularly its focus on empowering bureaucrats. He believes this will address bureaucratic paralysis and create a more inclusive economy.  **Narendra Modi**'s leadership has been lauded by business leaders for his clear vision and commitment to economic growth. **Mahindra & Mahindra** remains committed to investing in India despite economic downturns, citing the company's long-term perspective on the market. The company is also confident in its ability to capitalize on opportunities in defense and infrastructure development.  The US administration is urged to rebuild a strong relationship with India as it seeks to enhance its global role.

top_stories.title: Documents reveal contents of the first telegraph message between India & England - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: Newly discovered documents reveal the first telegraph messages sent from Porthcurno, England to Mumbai on June 23, 1870, marking a technological breakthrough in communication between Britain and its former colonies.  The **Managing Director** in London and the Manager in Bombay exchanged messages via undersea cables laid by the British Indian Submarine Telegraph Company. The first message was "How are you all?", which received a reply of "All well". This marked the beginning of a revolution that connected the world through telegraphy, with Porthcurno serving as a hub for international cable communications from 1870 to 1970 and later becoming a training college for the communications industry.  The museum, now housing rare equipment and details of the history of telegraph, has received millions in funding to develop an international education program that includes community groups in India.

top_stories.title: India Meteorological Department to use dynamic models for forecasts - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **M Rajeevan**, of the **National Atmospheric Research Laboratory**, highlighted the need for improved monsoon prediction models in light of the 2009 drought.  He noted that state-of-the-art coupled ocean atmospheric models have shown improvement in predicting interannual variability of Indian summer monsoon rainfall. **Michel Jarraud**, secretary general of the **World Meteorological Organisation**, emphasized the importance of global data, supercomputers, and translating scientific progress into practical applications for better weather forecasting.
